items.question: What is my educational background?
items.answer:
Rudra holds a Master of Computer Science from the University of Wollongong, Australia, completed between 2023 and 2025 with a major in Machine Learning and Big Data, awarded in August 2025 [[cite:2,8]]. This degree carried 96 credit points and was supported by the UOW Postgraduate Academic Excellence Scholarship, a 30% tuition fee waiver [[cite:8]].

Prior to this, he earned a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering from GSFC University in Vadodara, Gujarat, India, admitted in July 2019 and graduating in May 2023 [[cite:2,7]]. He received the Achiever's Award during the 2021-22 academic year for this degree [[cite:7]].

His coursework spanned foundational subjects like mathematics, programming, and data structures, along with core computer science topics such as operating systems, computer networks, and web technologies [[cite:3]]. He also studied electronics and hardware subjects including digital electronics and microprocessor interfacing, plus professional topics like entrepreneurship development and disaster management [[cite:3]].

At the postgraduate level, his subjects concentrated on machine learning, big data, computer vision, and security, aligning with his Machine Learning and Big Data major [[cite:4,6]]. Specific units included Computer Vision Algorithms and Systems, Modern Cryptography, Big Data Analytics, and AI and Cybersecurity [[cite:6]]. He graduated with High Distinctions in Programming and Data Structures, Web Development, Strategic Network Design, and his Professional Capstone Project, which was the largest single subject at 12 credit points [[cite:4]]. He also earned Distinctions in Big Data Analytics, Security Essentials, AI and Cybersecurity, and System Analysis and Project Management [[cite:4]].

items.question: What is the title of the patent?
items.answer: The patent is titled "Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network" [[cite:1,3]]. It was filed as Indian patent application number 202211058943 A [[cite:3,5]].

items.question: What is the patent application number?
items.answer: The patent application number is 202211058943 A, for the invention titled Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network [[cite:2,3,4]]. This patent was filed on 15 October 2022 with the Indian Patent Office and published in the Patent Office Journal No. 42/2022 dated 21 October 2022 [[cite:2,3]]. Rudra Joshi is listed as one of the applicants alongside Dr Kanta Prasad Sharma, Priyadarshi, Kshitij Joshi, Pujan Soni, and Pearl Miglani [[cite:7]].

items.question: What neural network architectures does the patent describe?
items.answer: The patent describes a face recognition system that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a recurrent neural network (RNN) [[cite:5]]. The CNN and RNN are used together in a key generation module that produces a consistent key value from sample facial images of a person [[cite:5]]. This architecture is formally titled the Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network in the patent filing [[cite:1,3]].

items.question: What is the patent journal number?
items.answer: The patent was published in the Patent Office Journal No. 42/2022, dated 21 October 2022 [[cite:1,3]].

items.question: What is the Cognitive-Chair project about?
items.answer:
The Cognitive-Chair is an AI-based brain-sensing wheelchair designed to assist paraplegic and quadriplegic individuals [[cite:5]]. It uses a Brain Sensing Headband along with electro-oculography to capture neural and eye-movement data, which is transferred to a mobile application and then relayed to the wheelchair so it can be controlled according to the user's neuro signal rather than physical input [[cite:4,5]]. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of both manual wheelchairs, which require physical strength and can cause strain injuries, and powered wheelchairs, which tend to be heavy, costly, and harder to transport [[cite:8]].

The project was carried out during Rudra Joshi's B.Tech at GSFC University and involved co-authors Kshitij Joshi, Abhilasha Vyas, Smit Joshi, and others, with Rudra Joshi as a co-author [[cite:1,5]]. It received the Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST-2022), organised by the Centre of Excellence - Artificial Intelligence, and was published on IEEE Xplore [[cite:5,7]]. The research also led to a related Indian government patent filing for an Intelligent Face Recognition System using Deep Recurrent Neural Network [[cite:1,5,6]].

items.question: What are the main brainwave frequencies mentioned?
items.answer: The main brainwave frequencies mentioned are Gamma, Beta, Alpha, Theta, and Delta [[cite:1,2]]. Gamma waves are associated with acquiring new information in the brain [[cite:1]]. Beta waves relate to focused attention on cognitive and real-world tasks and represent the typical conscious state [[cite:1]]. Alpha waves are linked to calm, pleasant thinking and are considered the brain's default resting state, aiding relaxation and alertness [[cite:1]]. Theta waves are most common during sleep and deep meditation [[cite:1]]. Delta waves have low frequency and are associated with deep tranquility, relaxation, and dream formation during the deepest states of sleep or meditation [[cite:1]].

items.question: What microcontroller is used in the wheelchair design?
items.answer: The wheelchair design uses an Arduino microcontroller to process data received from the Android application and control the wheelchair motors and other hardware [[cite:1]]. The system architecture links the mobile application, which runs the control algorithm, to this microcontroller to manage the wheelchair's movement [[cite:2]].

items.question: Which bluetooth module does the system use?
items.answer: The system uses the HC-06 bluetooth module for wireless transmission of signals between the headband and the microcontroller [[cite:2]]. This module functions by managing the wireless communication channel clearly and without delay, connecting to smartphones via a Bluetooth terminal application [[cite:1]].

items.question: What is a Brain-Computer Interface according to the paper?
items.answer: A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), also called Brain-Machine Interface or Direct Neural Interface, is a technology that lets users communicate with machines or external devices using brain signals instead of the normal peripheral nerve and muscle pathways, giving humans the ability to control machines directly [[cite:1]]. It is considered one of the most promising technologies for assisting and enhancing communication and control for people with motor paralysis caused by conditions such as paraplegia, quadriplegia, stroke, spinal cord injury, cerebral palsy, and ALS [[cite:2,7]]. A BCI system is composed of three main parts: electrodes that record electrical, magnetic, or metabolic brain activity, a processing pipeline that interprets these signals and decodes patterns into commands, and a computer or external device that executes those commands [[cite:5]]. BCIs are further classified into invasive, non-invasive, and semi-invasive types depending on how the electrodes interact with the brain [[cite:5]].
